scope: Standalone frozen verified known-identity RSS primitive and fourteen prepared mock methods only
source_judgment: Sampling accepts bounded typed PID/create_time inventories and requires a nonempty mandatory subset. Every sampled RSS is bracketed by fresh Process(pid) birth observations; replacement identities are not sampled after reuse is detected.

A NoSuchProcess observation triggers a separate fresh lookup. Only fresh absence or a different birth produces a departed row. Same original identity still present, AccessDenied, unknown exceptions and malformed metadata stop and retain sticky failure.

Departed rows retain the exact original identity and rss_bytes=null; known provenance is not deleted. Prior successful receipts and counts remain intact after a later failure. No departed memory value or learner/fit count is fabricated.

The caller's supplied checkpoint is invoked around OS observations and confirmation. Its exception identity is preserved and made sticky. The primitive contains no clock creation, cadence or last-successful-timestamp update; successful_rounds denotes completed sampling rounds, not a complete guard PASS.
Raw RSS values, including boundary and over-cap values, are returned unchanged. Memory-cap policy and the existing conservative parent double-count remain consumer responsibilities.

Owned-tree discovery traverses only one supplied root. New child births are not accepted if root scope becomes unconfirmed; a child whose birth cannot be observed causes STOP. There is no process_iter, arbitrary host discovery or authority to terminate any process.

Fourteen prepared mock methods meaningfully cover stable sampling, initial and post-RSS disappearance, reuse, same-birth contradiction, sticky denial/unknown/checkpoint failures, malformed identities, mandatory identity omission, raw cap values, prior receipt retention and owned-root discovery. Their bodies use injected fake process factories; none was executed during this review.
mandatory_consumer_review_boundaries: The API trusts the caller-supplied required identities; each actual consumer must pass its captured actual SELF identity as mandatory, rather than another trusted process alone.
Consumers must retain the original known identity inventory and accumulated peaks after departures, and must not reinterpret a departed null as an observed live RSS of zero.
Consumers may advance the original last-successful resource sample timestamp only after the mandatory SELF sample, all memory caps and original clock/gap checks complete successfully.
The callback must be the original non-reentrant clock-only checkpoint. Passing an RSS-sampling checkpoint would recurse and is not an approved integration.
Candidate, coordinator and controller integration, exact dependency/flat mapping and actual source tests remain separate frozen review and qualification steps.
conclusion: No concrete standalone primitive source blocker in the authorized scope; consumer invariants require the separately assigned source review
